events_chronological: Supermarket checkout girl Corey takes Marek's Christmas Eve shift because he is driving to the desert casino city and she is about to be evicted.
A narcotics detective named Kessel catches the soap actors Reid and Vaughn buying and puts them in wires to make a case against their dealer.
Reid and Vaughn come to Marek's till asking for twenty hits of ecstasy.
Corey takes the deal herself and goes with her friend Bett to Marek's dealer, Nyle.
Nyle refuses to front the drugs, so Corey leaves Bett in his flat as collateral and takes the pills on credit.
In the car park Corey spots Kessel waiting with Reid and Vaughn and realises the buy is a sting.
Corey flushes the ecstasy and sells the pair crushed cold remedies instead.
Marek and his friend Ozzie talk their way into a free suite, a wedding chapel and a strip club.
Marek sleeps with two women and leaves a hotel room on fire.
Kessel takes Reid and Vaughn home to dinner, where his real interest turns out to be signing them into a pyramid scheme with his wife Deb.
Corey goes to a warehouse rave to unload the rest of the aspirin on strangers.
Marek takes a security guard's gun in the club, shoots the bouncer through the arm, and the four run for the car.
The club's owner chases them out into the desert and shoots the borrowed sports car to pieces.
Nyle works out that he has been cheated and comes after Corey at the rave, and she runs out into the road.
Reid and Vaughn, driving home, are the ones who hit her, and they panic and leave her in an alley.
Marek gets back to town and Nyle corners him over the money, and Marek shoots Nyle through the arm.
Corey comes round in the alley and reaches the diner on Christmas morning, where all three stories meet.
nonlinear_category_reason: Three chapters, one per group of characters, each rewinding to the same supermarket shift.
syuzhet_notes: The film tells the same night three times over, once per group, rewinding to the supermarket at the start of each chapter. Told-order bullets 1-8 are the checkout girl's night, bullets 9-12 restart the evening in the casino city, and bullets 13-15 restart it again with the two actors, revealing that the car that hit her at bullet 8 was theirs. Only the last two bullets belong to a stretch all three strands share.
fabula_notes: The three chapters are largely simultaneous, so a single chronology has to interleave scenes the film keeps in separate blocks; the ordering here follows the few shared markers - the buy, the rave, the collision, the morning after. That the detective had already turned the two actors before they walked into the supermarket is only established in the third chapter.

events.content: He has counted the pills, and tasted one, and worked out what she did. He finds her in the crowd, and she goes out of the fire door and straight into the road.

reader: the debt comes due at the worst possible moment

events.content: They are driving home from a dinner they cannot explain when something comes out of a doorway into the headlights. They put her in an alley and drive on, and this is the moment the third chapter exists to deliver.

reader: the car that hit her belonged to the other strand all along

events.content: Back in town with no car and no money, he is cornered over a debt he never took on, and the evening ends with the supplier on the floor holding his arm and swearing.

reader: the two strands settle the same debt from opposite ends

events.content: She comes round between two bins on Christmas morning, walks the eight blocks, and pushes open a door behind which everybody from all three nights is eating breakfast.

reader: the three chapters arrive in one room
